#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Unit tests for the Dockerfile pin parser in check_deb_pins.sh.
#
# Only the text handling is tested here — no network, no container. The installability
# verdict itself is apt's, and is exercised by running check_deb_pins.sh for real.
set -uo pipefail

repo_root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "$repo_root/script/check_deb_pins.sh" --source-only

failures=0

expect_eq() {
  local name=$1 expected=$2 actual=$3
  if [[ $expected == "$actual" ]]; then
    echo "  ok   $name"
  else
    echo "  FAIL $name"
    echo "    expected: $(printf '%q' "$expected")"
    echo "    actual:   $(printf '%q' "$actual")"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

echo "== parse_pins =="

cat > "$tmp/basic.Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM debian:13.6-slim AS flutter
# renovate: depName=curl
ARG CURL_VERSION="8.14.1-2+deb13u4"
# renovate: depName=git
ARG GIT_VERSION="1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1"

FROM flutter AS android
# renovate: depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1"
EOF
expect_eq "pairs annotations with the following ARG, tracking stage" \
  "flutter curl 8.14.1-2+deb13u4
flutter git 1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1
android openjdk-17-jdk-headless 17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1" \
  "$(parse_pins "$tmp/basic.Dockerfile")"

# An epoch (1:...) and a Debian revision with ~ must survive intact — mangling either
# would silently check a different version than the image installs.
cat > "$tmp/versions.Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM debian:13.6-slim AS s
# renovate: depName=ruby-full
ARG RUBY_VERSION="1:3.3"
# renovate: depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1"
EOF
expect_eq "preserves epochs and ~ revisions verbatim" \
  "s ruby-full 1:3.3
s openjdk-17-jdk-headless 17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1" \
  "$(parse_pins "$tmp/versions.Dockerfile")"

# An ARG that is not preceded by an annotation is not a pin — build args like
# flutter_version must not be mistaken for one.
cat > "$tmp/unannotated.Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM debian:13.6-slim AS s
ARG SOME_OTHER_VERSION="9.9.9"
ARG flutter_version
# renovate: depName=sudo
ARG SUDO_VERSION="1.9.16p2-3+deb13u2"
EOF
expect_eq "ignores ARGs with no preceding annotation" \
  "s sudo 1.9.16p2-3+deb13u2" \
  "$(parse_pins "$tmp/unannotated.Dockerfile")"

cat > "$tmp/none.Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM debian:13.6-slim AS s
RUN echo hi
EOF
expect_eq "emits nothing when there are no pins" "" "$(parse_pins "$tmp/none.Dockerfile")"

echo "== sources_for_stage =="
expect_eq "android needs the bookworm sources" \
  "config/debian_12_bookworm.sources" "$(sources_for_stage android)"
expect_eq "flutter uses base image sources only" "" "$(sources_for_stage flutter)"
expect_eq "linux uses base image sources only" "" "$(sources_for_stage linux)"

echo
if [[ $failures -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "All parser tests passed."
else
  echo "$failures test(s) failed." >&2
fi
exit $((failures > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify every `# renovate:`-annotated apt pin is installable.
#
# Renovate cannot catch a bad pin on its own: it only ever proposes upgrades, so a pin
# sorting above the archive looks identical to a pin that is current (#555). Nor is it
# enough to check that the pinned version exists — openjdk-17-jdk-headless=17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2
# exists in bookworm yet cannot be installed, because bookworm-security ships a newer
# openjdk-17-jre-headless and the JDK declares Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= <same>).
#
# So this asks apt the question the build asks: can you install exactly this version?
# `apt-get install --simulate` runs the real solver against the stage's real sources.
set -euo pipefail

readonly BASE_IMAGE="debian:13.6-slim"
# Stages that add apt sources beyond the base image's own. Everything else resolves
# against trixie alone. Keep in sync with the COPY of a *.sources file in the Dockerfile.
readonly ANDROID_SOURCES="config/debian_12_bookworm.sources"

repo_root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
cd "$repo_root"

docker=${DOCKER:-docker}

fail_infra() {
  echo "ERROR (infrastructure): $*" >&2
  echo "This is not a pin problem — the check could not evaluate the pins." >&2
  exit 2
}

# Emit "<stage> <depName> <version>" for every annotated pin.
# The annotation names the package; the ARG on the next line carries the version. They are
# paired positionally, exactly as Renovate's custom manager matches them.
parse_pins() {
  local file=$1
  awk '
    /^FROM /       { stage = $NF }
    /^# renovate: depName=/ { dep = substr($0, index($0, "depName=") + 8); next }
    dep != "" && /^ARG [A-Z0-9_]+_VERSION=/ {
      v = substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1)
      gsub(/^"|"$/, "", v)
      print stage, dep, v
      dep = ""
    }
  ' "$file"
}

# Which sources file a stage needs, or empty for base-image-only.
# android inherits from fastlane <- flutter, and adds bookworm.
sources_for_stage() {
  case $1 in
    android) printf '%s' "$ANDROID_SOURCES" ;;
    *)       printf '' ;;
  esac
}

# Verify one group of pins against one sources file, inside a container.
# Returns 0 if every pin installs, 1 if any pin does not. Exits 2 on infrastructure failure.
check_group() {
  local sources=$1
  shift
  local pins=("$@")

  local label="base image sources (trixie)"
  [[ -n $sources ]] && label="base image sources + $sources"
  echo "==> Resolving ${#pins[@]} pin(s) against $label"

  # Inline the sources file into the script rather than bind-mounting it: a mount needs
  # SELinux relabelling under podman, and this keeps the check runtime-agnostic.
  local copy_cmd=":"
  if [[ -n $sources ]]; then
    [[ -f $sources ]] || fail_infra "sources file not found: $sources"
    copy_cmd=$(printf 'cat > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/extra.sources <<'"'"'EXTRA_SOURCES'"'"'\n%s\nEXTRA_SOURCES' "$(cat "$sources")")
  fi

  # One `apt-get update` per group, then one --simulate per pin. Report each pin's verdict
  # on its own line so the caller can separate "apt said no" from "apt never ran".
  local script
  script=$(cat <<EOF
set -u
$copy_cmd
for attempt in 1 2; do
  apt-get update -qq && break
  [ "\$attempt" = 2 ] && { echo "__APT_UPDATE_FAILED__"; exit 90; }
  sleep 3
done
status=0
while IFS='=' read -r pkg ver; do
  [ -z "\$pkg" ] && continue
  out=\$(apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends --simulate "\$pkg=\$ver" 2>&1) || {
    echo "__PIN_FAILED__ \$pkg \$ver"
    echo "\$out" | grep -E 'Depends:|E: |but .* is to be installed|Version .* not found|has no installation candidate' | sed 's/^/    /'
    cand=\$(apt-cache policy "\$pkg" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/ {print \$2}')
    [ -n "\$cand" ] && echo "    apt would install instead: \$cand"
    status=1
    continue
  }
  echo "__PIN_OK__ \$pkg \$ver"
done <<'PINS'
$(printf '%s\n' "${pins[@]}")
PINS
exit \$status
EOF
)

  local output rc
  set +e
  output=$("$docker" run --rm "$BASE_IMAGE" bash -c "$script" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e

  if grep -q '__APT_UPDATE_FAILED__' <<<"$output"; then
    fail_infra "apt-get update failed for $label (after one retry)"
  fi
  if [[ $rc -ne 0 && $rc -ne 1 ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2
    fail_infra "container exited $rc for $label"
  fi

  local group_status=0
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case $line in
      __PIN_OK__*)     echo "  ok   ${line#__PIN_OK__ }" ;;
      __PIN_FAILED__*) echo "  FAIL ${line#__PIN_FAILED__ }"; group_status=1 ;;
      "    "*)         echo "$line" ;;
    esac
  done <<<"$output"

  return $group_status
}

main() {
  command -v "$docker" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail_infra "$docker not found; this check needs a container runtime"

  shopt -s nullglob
  local dockerfiles=(*.Dockerfile)
  shopt -u nullglob
  [[ ${#dockerfiles[@]} -gt 0 ]] || fail_infra "no *.Dockerfile found in $repo_root"

  # Group pins by the sources file their stage needs, so each group costs one apt-get update.
  local base_pins=() android_pins=() total=0
  local stage dep version
  while read -r stage dep version; do
    [[ -z ${stage:-} ]] && continue
    total=$((total + 1))
    if [[ -n $(sources_for_stage "$stage") ]]; then
      android_pins+=("$dep=$version")
    else
      base_pins+=("$dep=$version")
    fi
  done < <(for f in "${dockerfiles[@]}"; do parse_pins "$f"; done)

  # A run that checks nothing must not look like a run that found nothing wrong. If the
  # annotation shape changes and the parser stops matching, that is a failure, not a pass.
  if [[ $total -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: no '# renovate:' apt pins found in ${dockerfiles[*]}" >&2
    echo "The parser matched nothing — either the pins are gone or the annotation shape changed." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  local status=0
  if [[ ${#base_pins[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    check_group "" "${base_pins[@]}" || status=1
  fi
  if [[ ${#android_pins[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    check_group "$ANDROID_SOURCES" "${android_pins[@]}" || status=1
  fi

  echo
  if [[ $status -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "All $total apt pin(s) are installable."
  else
    echo "Some apt pins cannot be installed. Repin to a version apt can resolve —" >&2
    echo "read the candidate from the output above, not from a failing build's error text." >&2
  fi
  return $status
}

main "$@"

jobs:
  # Resolves the bootstrap container tag — the latest published release tag.
  # Reading from the releases API (instead of vars.FLUTTER_VERSION) makes
  # fork PRs work, and reading from releases (instead of main's version.json)
  # avoids the window between merging a version-bump PR and publishing its
  # image during which main's version.json points to a tag that doesn't
  # exist in GHCR yet.
  setup:
    name: Read latest release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      flutter_version: ${{ steps.read.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Read latest release tag
        id: read
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/releases/latest" --jq '.tag_name')
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build-image:
    name: Build and push image (${{ matrix.name }})
    permissions:
      packages: write
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # One leg per published Linux-hosted image from android.Dockerfile. `target`
    # selects its stage and `name` the published repository.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: flutter-android
            target: android
          - name: flutter-web
            target: web
          - name: flutter-linux
            target: linux
    # These are image-independent, so the last-leg-wins behaviour of matrix job
    # outputs is harmless: every leg computes the same handoff for test/scan. The
    # per-image digest is not image-independent, so scan-image recomputes it.

- **GIVEN** the `fastlane` gem, whose version is owned by `config/version.json` and injected via `--build-arg fastlane_version`
- **WHEN** a maintainer scans `android.Dockerfile` for `# renovate:` annotations
- **THEN** no annotation names `fastlane` as a `depName`
- **AND** Renovate does not surface `fastlane` as a managed dependency of the Dockerfile

### Requirement: Each apt pin resolves against the same set of Debian suites the image enables

Every `deb`-datasource pin SHALL be resolved against the full set of apt suites enabled in the image stage that installs it — the base suite, its `-updates` suite, and its `-security` suite — expressed as a list of `registryUrls` on a `packageRules` entry in `.github/renovate.json`. Each `registryUrls` entry SHALL mirror exactly one `Types`/`URIs`/`Suites`/`Components` stanza of the image's real apt sources, in both suite and component list. Suite selection SHALL NOT be expressed via `registryUrlTemplate`, which renders a single URL and therefore cannot address a set.

**Experience context:** A CI engineer trusts that a Renovate PR bumping an apt pin produces a version the image can actually install. apt picks the highest version across every enabled suite, so if Renovate watches fewer suites than apt, the two disagree about what "latest" is. That disagreement is what broke the image: `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` was pinned to `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2` while apt's candidate for its strict-equality dependency `openjdk-17-jre-headless` had moved to `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1` in `bookworm-security`, and the build failed with `E: Unable to correct problems, you have held broken packages`. Security uploads for an oldstable suite land in `-security` before they are folded into the main archive at a point release, so watching only the base suite guarantees this skew recurs. Mirroring the sources stanza-for-stanza also keeps the invariant auditable: a maintainer can read the rule beside the sources file and see they agree.

#### Scenario: A pin is resolved against base, updates and security suites

- **GIVEN** an apt pin in `android.Dockerfile` installed from a suite the image enables
- **WHEN** Renovate looks the package up
- **THEN** it queries that suite, its `-updates` suite, and its `-security` suite
- **AND** the candidate it proposes is the highest version across all of them — the version apt would install

#### Scenario: A pin installed from an added repository resolves against that repository

- **GIVEN** `openjdk-17-jdk-headless`, which the android stage installs after adding `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources`
- **WHEN** Renovate looks it up
- **THEN** it queries the bookworm suites named in that sources file, not the base image's trixie suites
- **AND** a security-only update published to `bookworm-security` is offered as an upgrade PR

#### Scenario: Suites are named by codename, not by a moving alias

- **GIVEN** the deb `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json`
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the configured suites
- **THEN** each names a Debian codename (e.g. `trixie`, `bookworm-security`)
- **AND** none uses a floating alias such as `stable` or `oldstable`, which would silently retarget every pin when Debian promotes a new release

### Requirement: Renovate configuration is syntax-validated before it is pushed

`.github/renovate.json` SHALL be syntax-validatable through a documented repository task that a maintainer can run locally. That task SHALL NOT be duplicated as a CI job.

## Implementation Complete

**Change:** renovate-deb-pin-resolution-guard
**Progress:** 21/24 tasks complete — the 3 remaining are PR-opening and post-merge verification, which need your call

### What landed

**`renovate-guard-work`** (5 commits, off `origin/main`):
- `3c8260f` — repin to `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`
- `7ff419d` — design/spec revision after the cold build
- `928250e` — the guard: `script/check_deb_pins.sh`, tests, mise tasks, CI wiring
- `0c08691` — spec sync

**`renovate/reconfigure`** (1 commit, off `origin/main`): `0656a11` — the renovate.json edit, isolated per project convention.

### The design change mid-implementation

Task 1 disproved the plan. The base-suite version I'd verified two ways *exists* but doesn't install — `bookworm-security` moved `openjdk-17-jre-headless` to `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, and the strict equality `Depends` forces the JDK to match. So the guard checks **installability** via `apt-get install --simulate`, validated against all three versions:

| Pin | Renovate | Exists | apt installs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1` (#555) | silent | no | no |
| `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2` | n/a | **yes** | **no** |
| `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1` | n/a | yes | **yes** |

The existence check I originally specified would have gone green on row 2 and left the image broken.

This also reversed the plan to drop the `-security` registryUrls: that's where the only installable version lives. Dropping them would have made the config contradict where the pin resolves from — the same false-premise-in-config that caused #555. Only `-updates` is dropped.

### Verification

- Guard green on all 14 pins; red on both bad values, printing apt's own `Depends:` explanation plus `apt would install instead: 17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`
- 7 parser tests pass, and confirmed to fail when the parser is broken — not vacuously green
- Three exit codes: 0 pass, 1 bad pin, 2 infrastructure
- `gx lint` clean, `renovate_validate.sh` passes, `openspec validate` passes for both items (5 other failures pre-exist on `origin/main`)

Two notes: I added a weekly `schedule` to `ci.yml` because a pin can rot with no repo change — exactly what happened here. And I reset the stale local `renovate/reconfigure` onto `origin/main` after confirming its content shipped as squash-merged #538, with no remote branch or open PR.

=== ci.yml trigger ===
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths-ignore:
      - changelog.md
  # A pin can go stale with no repo change at all: a security upload moves apt's candidate
  # and a strict `Depends: (= <version>)` makes the pinned version uninstallable (#555).
  # Without a periodic check that break is found by whoever next edits the Dockerfile.
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

# Read-only permissions by default
permissions:
  contents: read

# CI on main: latest commit wins; cancel superseded runs.

=== the job it fires ===
jobs:
  check-deb-pins:
    name: Check apt pins are installable
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Harden runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Checkout repository

content.text:
`cron: "17 6 * * 1"` — Mondays at 06:17 UTC, on `main`. Off-the-hour minute because GitHub drops scheduled runs that pile up at :00.

**Why it exists.** The PR-triggered guard in `build.yml` catches a bad pin when someone *writes* one. But #555 had a second mechanism: nobody touched the Dockerfile at all. Debian published a security upload, apt's candidate for `openjdk-17-jre-headless` moved, and the strict `Depends: (= <version>)` made the already-committed pin uninstallable. The repo went from building to not building with zero commits.

```
  PR guard        catches: someone writes a bad pin
  weekly guard    catches: an upload invalidates a good pin  ← no commit involved
```

Without it, that break surfaces whenever someone next edits `android.Dockerfile` — which was three weeks here, and would have been longer if #555 hadn't been filed.

**What a run does.** Checks out `main`, runs the parser tests, then resolves all 14 pins against the real archive — two containers, one `apt-get update` each, no image build, no Flutter SDK. Roughly a minute. Green means silence; red means a red X on `main` naming the dep and the version apt would install instead.

One caveat worth stating plainly: **it fires on `main` only**, so it reports the break, it doesn't prevent it — and a scheduled failure is a notification, not a blocked merge. Whether that reaches you depends on your GitHub notification settings for failed workflow runs on your own repo.

Also note GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days of repository inactivity, and re-enables on the next push. For an actively maintained repo that's a non-issue; worth knowing if the project goes quiet.

Two things I'd flag as judgment calls you may want to overrule:

- **Weekly cadence** is a guess. Debian security uploads for a given package are infrequent, but the window between an upload and your discovery is up to 7 days. Daily costs ~30x more runs for a tighter window.
- **It lives in `ci.yml`** alongside the image tests, so a pin failure shows up under "CI" rather than its own workflow. Cleaner in the actions list; slightly less obvious what failed.

content.text:
There's the mechanism: `Using cache` on the `apt-get install` step. Docker never contacted Debian.

**Where you're right:** on the PR path, the guard's value is thin. If a PR *edits* the `ARG` line, the Dockerfile text changes, the cache key changes, and Docker re-runs `apt-get install` — it would fail on a bad pin. The guard mostly buys a faster, clearer error there.

**Where the two diverge** is the case that actually produced #555 — nobody edits the file:

```
Dockerfile unchanged  ->  cache key unchanged  ->  "Using cache"
                                                    apt never runs
                                                    Debian never contacted
                                                    build goes GREEN
```

Meanwhile the pin has become uninstallable because a security upload moved the candidate. That's precisely what happened: `main` was broken and every build stayed green for three weeks — including PR #529's own CI, which is why its author's "CI on this PR is the verification" didn't hold. The cache key is the *Dockerfile text*; it has no idea Debian's archive moved underneath it.

So the answer to "does Docker already do this check": it does when the text changes, and it specifically does *not* when only the archive changes. The weekly run covers exactly that gap.

**But your challenge lands on the PR job.** Two overlapping checks is real duplication, and I should flag the honest counter-argument to my own design: a cold-build CI leg would catch both cases *and* catch things `--simulate` can't (postinstall failures, runtime breakage). I ruled it out in design.md for cost — a full uncached build per PR — but that reasoning is weaker for a scheduled weekly run, where cost barely matters.

Three ways to go:

1. **Keep both** (current). PR job gives fast, specific errors; weekly covers archive drift.
2. **Weekly only** — drop the `build.yml` job. Removes the duplication you're pointing at; a bad pin in a PR still fails, just via the slower Docker error.
3. **Weekly cold build instead of the guard** — strictly more coverage, much slower, and no "apt would install instead" hint.

I'd lean 2 if the duplication bothers you: it keeps the coverage Docker genuinely lacks and drops the part that mostly re-checks what a cache miss already catches. Want me to make that change?

content.text:
No — removing the cache would be a bad trade, and it wouldn't even fix the problem you're circling.

**What you'd pay.** The cache isn't protecting the apt layer; it's protecting a Flutter SDK git clone, a fastlane `gem install`, an Android cmdline-tools download, and `sdkmanager` pulling platform-tools + NDK + CMake. That's the bulk of a multi-GB image, on every PR, across three matrix legs. You'd be adding a large, network-flaky cost to every build.

**What you wouldn't get.** Removing the cache makes builds cold-*today*, but it doesn't make staleness *detected*. The failure mode is still time-based: the pin rots when Debian publishes, not when someone opens a PR. With no cache and no scheduled run, you'd still only find out whenever the next PR happens to land — same three-week window, just with slower builds throughout. Caching wasn't the cause; it was the anesthetic.

There's also a memory note from this repo worth heeding here: cold builds break locally for unrelated reasons (rubygems.org egress is flaky from this machine), so "always cold" makes the build less reproducible, not more.

The real trade is:

| | Cost | Catches archive drift |
|---|---|---|
| Remove cache | large, every PR × 3 legs | only when a PR happens |
| Scheduled check | ~1 min/week | yes, on a fixed cadence |

The cache makes builds fast and repeatable. A scheduled check makes staleness visible. Those are different jobs, and the second one is cheap.

My recommendation stands where it was two messages ago: **keep the cache, keep the weekly run, and drop the per-PR guard job** — that's option 2, and it removes the duplication you flagged without paying for cold builds. The PR path is already covered, because editing the `ARG` changes the cache key and forces `apt-get install` to re-run.

Want me to drop the `build.yml` job?

That settles it. **Docker already catches this on the PR path**, and the cache does not save it — editing the `ARG` changes the cache key, apt re-runs, the build fails.

So: **no meaningful added benefit.** You were right, and I should have tested this before building it rather than after.

The full picture, now that we've removed the schedule:

| Scenario | Docker build (PR) | check-deb-pins |
|---|---|---|
| PR edits pin to a bad value | **fails** | fails |
| Pin rots, no repo change | passes (cached) | passes (only runs on PRs) |

The second row is why the guard existed — and dropping the schedule removed the only trigger that covered it. What's left is a job that re-checks what the build in the same workflow already checks, a few minutes earlier and with a nicer message.

Three things it still does that the build doesn't, and I don't think any of them justify it:

- Prints `apt would install instead: <candidate>`. Genuinely useful — that one line is what identified the real fix in this session. But it's a nicety over a build failure that already names the problem.
- Checks all 14 pins including `linux`/`web` stage pins. The matrix builds those too.
- Fails in ~1 min vs. waiting on the image build. Real, minor.

My recommendation: **drop `check-deb-pins` entirely** — script, tests, mise tasks, and the `build.yml` job. Keep the repin (`3c8260f`), which is the actual fix for #555 and is independently verified. Keep the renovate.json cleanup on its own branch. The spec would need reworking too, since its new requirement is premised on a guard that isn't earning its place.

That leaves the real conclusion from this investigation, which doesn't need new machinery: **#555 happened because PR #529 was merged without a passing build on the edited pin.** Docker would have caught it. The gap was process, not tooling.

input.content:
## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Each apt pin resolves against the same set of Debian suites the image enables

Every `deb`-datasource pin SHALL be resolved against the Debian suites from which the
installing image stage can install it — at minimum the base suite and its `-security` suite —
expressed as a list of `registryUrls` on a `packageRules` entry in `.github/renovate.json`.
Each `registryUrls` entry SHALL mirror a `Types`/`URIs`/`Suites`/`Components` stanza of the
image's real apt sources, in both suite and component list. Suite selection SHALL NOT be
expressed via `registryUrlTemplate`, which renders a single URL and therefore cannot address a
set.

Where a listed suite cannot currently be fetched by Renovate, the configuration SHALL record
why in its `description`, naming the upstream limitation, so that a maintainer reading the
config can tell an intentional gap from an oversight.

**Experience context:** A CI engineer trusts that a Renovate PR bumping an apt pin produces a
version the image can actually install. apt picks the highest version across every enabled
suite, so if Renovate watches fewer suites than apt, the two disagree about what "latest" is.

`-security` is load-bearing, not merely a currency concern. The only installable version of
`openjdk-17-jdk-headless` is `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, published in `bookworm-security` and
nowhere else: a security upload moved `openjdk-17-jre-headless` there, and the JDK's strict
`Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= <same version>)` forces the JDK to follow. A configuration
omitting the `-security` suite would state that the pin comes from somewhere it does not, and
could never propose the version the image needs.

Renovate cannot currently fetch those suites: its deb datasource hardcodes
`const compression = 'gz'`, and Debian publishes only `Packages` and `Packages.xz` on
`-security` and `-updates`, so each such URL returns 404 on every run — swallowed at debug
level while the job reports success. This is upstream renovate#44330; no repository
configuration works around it, and no mirror still carries the `.gz`. The `-security` entries
are kept regardless, because they state correctly where the pin resolves from and will resume
working with no edit once upstream lands `.xz`. The `-updates` entries are dropped: they are
equally unfetchable and no current pin resolves from them, so they assert coverage with no
corresponding need.

While that gap persists, Renovate cannot be relied on to notice a pin that has stopped being
installable. What catches it is the image build itself: editing a pin changes the Dockerfile,
which invalidates the build cache and re-runs `apt-get install`, so a bad pin fails the PR that
introduces it. A pin can still rot with no repo change — a later security upload moves apt's
candidate — and that break surfaces on the next PR to touch the file rather than when it
happens. That delay is accepted.

#### Scenario: A pin is resolved against the base and security suites of its family

- **GIVEN** an apt pin in `android.Dockerfile` installed from a suite the image enables
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the configured `registryUrls` for that pin
- **THEN** they name the base suite and its `-security` suite
- **AND** together they describe where apt actually resolves the package from

#### Scenario: A pin installed from an added repository resolves against that repository

- **GIVEN** `openjdk-17-jdk-headless`, which the android stage installs after adding `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources`
- **WHEN** Renovate looks it up
- **THEN** it queries the bookworm suites named in that sources file, not the base image's trixie suites

#### Scenario: A known upstream fetch limitation is documented, not silent

- **GIVEN** a configured suite Renovate cannot currently fetch
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the deb `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json`
- **THEN** the `description` names the upstream limitation preventing it from being fetched
- **AND** the entry is recognisable as an intentional gap rather than a stale mistake

#### Scenario: A pin edited to an uninstallable version fails its own pull request

- **GIVEN** a pull request that changes an apt pin to a version apt cannot install
- **WHEN** the image is built for that pull request
- **THEN** the changed Dockerfile invalidates the build cache, `apt-get install` re-runs, and the build fails
- **AND** the failure names the version and the unmet dependency, so the pin is corrected before merge

#### Scenario: Suites are named by codename, not by a moving alias

- **GIVEN** the deb `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json`
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the configured suites
- **THEN** each names a Debian codename (e.g. `trixie`, `bookworm-security`)
- **AND** none uses a floating alias such as `stable` or `oldstable`, which would silently retarget every pin when Debian promotes a new release

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Every apt pin names a version the image can actually install

Every `deb`-datasource pin in a `*.Dockerfile` SHALL name a version that apt can install from
the suites the installing image stage enables, with all of that package's dependency
constraints satisfied. A repository check SHALL assert this for all such pins and SHALL fail
when any pinned version cannot be installed.

The check SHALL evaluate **installability**, not existence and not currency:

- A pin naming a version published in no enabled suite SHALL fail.
- A pin naming a version that is published but whose dependencies cannot be satisfied SHALL
  also fail.
- A pin naming an installable version that is not the newest available SHALL pass; proposing
  newer versions remains Renovate's responsibility.

The check SHALL report a failure caused by an unreachable or unreadable package index
distinctly from a failure caused by a pin that apt refuses to install, and SHALL NOT report
success for any pin it could not evaluate.

**Experience context:** A CI engineer expects `main` to build. Two distinct defects broke that
expectation, and only the second predicate catches both.

`openjdk-17-jdk-headless` was pinned to `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1`, published in no enabled suite.
The image stopped building and nothing reported it for three weeks. Renovate could not: it
fetched the bookworm index, read the ceiling `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2`, and stayed silent because
`17.0.20` sorts above `17.0.19` and Renovate only ever proposes upgrades. Its silence means
"your pin is current" **or** "your pin cannot be installed", and the repository had no way to
tell those apart. Warm build caches hid it further — no CI path re-executed the
`apt-get install` layer, so the PR introducing the pin went green without testing it.

Repinning to the base-suite version `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2` — which does exist — **still did not
build**. `bookworm-security` carries `openjdk-17-jre-headless=17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, apt takes
it as the candidate, and `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` declares a strict
`Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= <same version>)`, so the JDK must match the security JRE.
A check asking only "does this version exist" would have passed that pin and left the image
broken. The version a CI engineer needs is the one apt can install, so that is what is checked.

#### Scenario: A pin naming a nonexistent version fails

- **GIVEN** a pin `openjdk-17-jdk-headless="17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1"`, published in no enabled suite
- **WHEN** the check runs
- **THEN** it fails
- **AND** it reports the dependency name, the pinned value, and the apt sources it resolved against

#### Scenario: A pin that exists but cannot be installed fails

- **GIVEN** a pin `openjdk-17-jdk-headless="17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2"`, published in `bookworm` but whose strict dependency on `openjdk-17-jre-headless` at the same version cannot be satisfied because `bookworm-security` supplies a newer one
- **WHEN** the check runs
- **THEN** it fails, even though the pinned version exists in an enabled suite
- **AND** it reports the unsatisfied dependency and the version apt would install instead, so the correct pin is readable from the output

#### Scenario: An installable pin behind the newest version passes

- **GIVEN** a pin naming a version that apt can install but that is no longer the newest available
- **WHEN** the check runs
- **THEN** it passes, because the image can build with it
- **AND** proposing the newer version remains Renovate's responsibility, not the check's

#### Scenario: An unreachable index is reported as an infrastructure failure

- **GIVEN** the check cannot retrieve or read a package index — network failure, HTTP error, or a failed index refresh
- **WHEN** it evaluates the pins covered by that index
- **THEN** it fails with an error distinguishing "the index could not be read" from "apt refuses to install this version"
- **AND** it never reports success for pins it was unable to evaluate

#### Scenario: Checking zero pins is a failure

- **GIVEN** the check finds no `# renovate:`-annotated pins to verify, for example after a Dockerfile refactor changes the annotation shape
- **WHEN** it runs
- **THEN** it fails rather than reporting success
- **AND** a passing run lists each pin checked and the apt sources it resolved against, so coverage is read from the output rather than assumed

#### Scenario: A maintainer runs the same check locally

- **GIVEN** a maintainer editing an apt pin
- **WHEN** they run the repository task for the check
- **THEN** it performs the same verification CI performs, with no setup beyond the repository's own tooling

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Each apt pin resolves against the same set of Debian suites the image enables

Every `deb`-datasource pin SHALL be resolved against the Debian suites from which the
installing image stage can install it — at minimum the base suite and its `-security` suite —
expressed as a list of `registryUrls` on a `packageRules` entry in `.github/renovate.json`.
Each `registryUrls` entry SHALL mirror a `Types`/`URIs`/`Suites`/`Components` stanza of the
image's real apt sources, in both suite and component list. Suite selection SHALL NOT be
expressed via `registryUrlTemplate`, which renders a single URL and therefore cannot address a
set.

Where a listed suite cannot currently be fetched by Renovate, the configuration SHALL record
why in its `description`, naming the upstream limitation, so that a maintainer reading the
config can tell an intentional gap from an oversight.

**Experience context:** A CI engineer trusts that a Renovate PR bumping an apt pin produces a
version the image can actually install. apt picks the highest version across every enabled
suite, so if Renovate watches fewer suites than apt, the two disagree about what "latest" is.

`-security` is load-bearing, not merely a currency concern. The only installable version of
`openjdk-17-jdk-headless` is `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, which is published in `bookworm-security`
and nowhere else: a security upload moved `openjdk-17-jre-headless` there, and the JDK's strict
equality dependency forces the JDK to follow. A configuration that omitted the `-security`
suite would state that the pin comes from somewhere it does not, and could never propose the
version the image needs.

Renovate cannot currently fetch those suites: its deb datasource hardcodes
`const compression = 'gz'`, and Debian publishes only `Packages` and `Packages.xz` on
`-security` and `-updates`, so each such URL returns 404 on every run — swallowed at debug
level while the job reports success. This is upstream renovate#44330; no repository
configuration works around it, and no mirror still carries the `.gz`. The `-security` entries
are kept regardless, because they state correctly where the pin resolves from and will resume
working with no edit once upstream lands `.xz`. The `-updates` entries are dropped: they are
equally unfetchable and no current pin resolves from them, so they assert coverage with no
corresponding need.

The installability check above is what protects correctness while the gap persists — it fails
the moment apt's candidate moves out from under a pin, which is precisely how the
`-security`-only version became mandatory.

#### Scenario: A pin is resolved against the base and security suites of its family

- **GIVEN** an apt pin in `android.Dockerfile` installed from a suite the image enables
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the configured `registryUrls` for that pin
- **THEN** they name the base suite and its `-security` suite
- **AND** together they describe where apt actually resolves the package from

#### Scenario: A pin installed from an added repository resolves against that repository

- **GIVEN** `openjdk-17-jdk-headless`, which the android stage installs after adding `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources`
- **WHEN** Renovate looks it up
- **THEN** it queries the bookworm suites named in that sources file, not the base image's trixie suites

#### Scenario: A known upstream fetch limitation is documented, not silent

- **GIVEN** a configured suite Renovate cannot currently fetch
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the deb `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json`
- **THEN** the `description` names the upstream limitation preventing it from being fetched
- **AND** the entry is recognisable as an intentional gap rather than a stale mistake

#### Scenario: Suites are named by codename, not by a moving alias

- **GIVEN** the deb `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json`
- **WHEN** a maintainer reads the configured suites
- **THEN** each names a Debian codename (e.g. `trixie`, `bookworm-security`)
- **AND** none uses a floating alias such as `stable` or `oldstable`, which would silently retarget every pin when Debian promotes a new release

## Why

`android.Dockerfile` pinned `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` to `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1`, a version
published in no Debian suite the image enables
([#555](https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/555)). `main` could not
cold-build for three weeks.

Renovate stayed silent throughout, and that is worth recording but is not the failure: the pin
sorts *above* the archive ceiling under deb versioning, and Renovate only ever proposes
upgrades, so a pin ahead of the archive is indistinguishable to it from one that is current.

The actual failure was in review, not tooling. Editing a pin changes the Dockerfile, which
invalidates the build cache and re-runs `apt-get install` — so the image build **does** catch a
bad pin on the PR that introduces one. PR #529 stated "CI on this PR is the verification" and
was merged without that verification passing on the edited pin.

Repinning to the base-suite version `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2` also fails: `bookworm-security`
carries `openjdk-17-jre-headless=17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, apt takes it as the candidate, and the
JDK's strict `Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= <same version>)` forces the JDK to match. The
only installable version is the security one.

This meets the relevance gate: a CI engineer building these images is directly affected — the
image does not build — and where a pin resolves from is a property of the published images.

## What Changes

- **Repin** `OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION` to `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, the
  `bookworm-security` version, verified by a `--no-cache` build of the apt layer rather than by
  reading apt error output. Restores cold builds.
- **Drop the two `-updates` `registryUrls`** from `.github/renovate.json` and **keep the
  `-security` entries**, documenting in the `description` that Renovate cannot currently fetch
  them. Renovate hardcodes `const compression = 'gz'` and Debian publishes no `Packages.gz` on
  either, so all four 404 on every run — swallowed at debug level. But `-security` is where the
  only installable openjdk version lives, so removing it would make the config contradict where
  the pin comes from; `-updates` supplies no current pin. Blocked upstream on
  [renovate#44330](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/44330) /
  [PR #35865](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/pull/35865).
- **Correct the `linux-image-package-pinning` spec**, whose experience context asserts that
  `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1` was a real `bookworm-security` upload and has the two versions swapped.
  That exact version was not published anywhere; it appears to be an imprecise transcription of
  `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, which is real — and that imprecision is what broke the build. The
  requirement also mandates resolving against `-updates` and `-security`, which no
  configuration can satisfy with current Renovate.

**No new CI check.** A dedicated pin-verification script was built and then removed: it
duplicated what the image build already does on the PR path, and its one non-duplicated case
(a pin rotting with no repo change) was judged not worth a scheduled job — finding that on the
next PR is the intended workflow.

**Not breaking.** No published image tag, entrypoint, or documented interface changes. The
repin moves the installed JDK to the version apt would actually select.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

_None._

### Modified Capabilities

- `linux-image-package-pinning`: Amends *"Each apt pin resolves against the same set of Debian
  suites the image enables"* — narrowing the mandate from base + `-updates` + `-security` (not
  satisfiable: four of six configured URLs cannot be fetched) to base + `-security`, requiring
  the unfetchable gap to be documented rather than silent, and correcting the experience
  context's false premise. Adds a scenario recording that the image build is what catches an
  uninstallable pin on its own PR.

## Impact

- `android.Dockerfile` — one `ARG` value (the repin).
- `.github/renovate.json` — remove two `-updates` `registryUrls` entries, expand two
  `description` fields. Per project convention this file changes only on a
  `renovate/reconfigure` branch, so it ships as its own PR.
- `openspec/specs/linux-image-package-pinning/spec.md` — amended requirement + corrected
  experience context.
- No workflow, script, or tooling changes. No change to image contents beyond the JDK version,
  and none to build cache keys, tags, or release flow.
EOF

cat > openspec/changes/renovate-deb-pin-resolution-guard/design.md <<'EOF'
## Context

`android.Dockerfile` pinned `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` to `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1`, published in no
suite the image enables. `main` could not cold-build for three weeks (#555).

Renovate stayed silent. A cache-cold local run of Renovate 44.46.0 (research.md §4) shows it
*did* fetch the bookworm index and *did* read the ceiling `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2`, then emitted
`updates: []` because
`isGreaterThan('17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1', '17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2') === true`. Renovate proposes
upgrades only, so a pin above the archive is indistinguishable from one that is current.

A second defect surfaced while verifying the fix. The obvious repin target — the base-suite
`17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2`, which genuinely exists in bookworm — **also does not build**:

```
openjdk-17-jdk-headless : Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= 17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2)
                          but 17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1 is to be installed
```

`bookworm-security` published `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1` on 2026-08-18. apt selects it for the
JRE, and the JDK's strict equality dependency forces the JDK to match. The only installable pin
is the security one.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Restore cold-buildability of `main`.
- Stop `.github/renovate.json` from mandating suite coverage no configuration can deliver, and
  from omitting the suite the working pin actually comes from.
- Correct the spec's record of what happened.

**Non-Goals:**
- **A dedicated pin-verification CI check.** One was built and removed — see Decision 1.
- Restoring `-updates` / `-security` fetch coverage. Blocked upstream
  ([renovate#44330](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/44330)); no config works
  around a hardcoded `const compression = 'gz'`.
- Fixing the hardcoded-`17` / derived-major collision in `android.Dockerfile:162`. Tracked in
  [#536](https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/536).
- Removing the build cache. It protects a Flutter SDK clone, a `gem install`, and an Android
  SDK download; it is not what let #555 through.

## Decisions

### 1. No new CI check — the image build already covers the PR path

A `check_deb_pins.sh` guard was implemented, tested, wired into `build.yml`, and then removed.
The reasoning is worth keeping, because the guard was intuitively appealing and wrong.

The claim it rested on was that CI never re-executes `apt-get install`. That is true only while
the Dockerfile is unchanged. **Editing a pin changes the file, which changes the layer cache
key, which forces `apt-get install` to re-run** — verified directly: with a warm cache from a
good build, changing the `ARG` to a bad version fails the build with
`E: Version '...' was not found`. `build.yml` builds the android stage on every PR, so a pin
edited to an uninstallable value fails its own PR.

That leaves one non-duplicated case: a pin rotting with **no repo change**, when a security
upload moves apt's candidate underneath a committed pin. Only a scheduled run covers it. That
was considered and rejected — finding the break on the next PR is the intended workflow here,
so a recurring job and notification path buys a narrower detection window the project does not
need.

With the scheduled run gone, the guard checked only what the build in the same workflow already
checked, a few minutes earlier. Removed.

_What was actually lost:_ a specific error naming `apt would install instead: <candidate>`,
which is the line that identified the real fix in this investigation. The build failure names
the unmet dependency but not the candidate. Judged a nicety, not a justification.

_Conclusion drawn instead:_ #555 was a review failure, not a tooling gap. PR #529 said "CI on
this PR is the verification" and was merged without that verification passing.

### 2. Keep the `-security` registryUrls; drop only `-updates`

The correct pin for `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` lives in `bookworm-security`
(`17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`). Security coverage is a *correctness* concern for this package, not
merely currency — dropping those URLs would mean Renovate can never propose the version the
image needs.

But the URLs cannot be fetched either: Renovate hardcodes `const compression = 'gz'` and Debian
publishes no `Packages.gz` on `-security` or `-updates`. Both keeping and dropping are wrong in
different ways, and neither is fixable from config.

Resolution: **keep `-security`, drop `-updates`**, and make the gap explicit in the
`description` rather than in silence.

- Keeping `-security` costs 404s that were already happening, and encodes the correct intent —
  when renovate#44330 lands, coverage resumes with no edit.
- Dropping `-updates` removes URLs that are both unfetchable *and* not where any pin resolves
  from.

_Alternative considered:_ drop all four. Rejected once the security version turned out to be
load-bearing — the config would then contradict where the pin comes from, which is the same
class of false-premise-in-config that produced #555.

### 3. Verify the repin by cold-building the apt layer, not by reading apt output

#529 took its value from a failing build's error text and could not confirm it. The replacement
was verified by building the actual apt layer with `--no-cache` against the real bookworm
sources, confirming both that the base-suite version fails and that the security version
installs (`openjdk version "17.0.20.1"`).

## Automated Test Strategy

No new automated tests. The verification that matters already exists: `build.yml` builds the
android stage on every PR, and a changed pin forces `apt-get install` to re-run. The repin was
verified by a `--no-cache` build of the apt layer before committing.

The `renovate.json` change is syntax-checked by `mise run lint`
(`renovate-config-validator`), and authoritatively validated by the Renovate app itself on the
`renovate/reconfigure` branch. Neither checks that a suite is fetchable — that is what the
`description` comments and this design record instead.

## Observability

The `-security` URLs still 404 on every Renovate run, swallowed at debug level. That remains
invisible in the job summary, and no repository change can surface it while the upstream gap
persists. It is recorded in the `description` fields so the next reader of the config finds the
explanation where they will look for it, rather than rediscovering it from a job log.

An uninstallable pin is observable where it matters: as a failed image build on the PR that
introduces it, naming the version and the unmet dependency.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- **A pin can rot with no repo change** — a security upload moves apt's candidate and the
  committed pin stops being installable → Surfaces on the next PR touching the Dockerfile
  rather than when it happens. Accepted deliberately; this is the delay #555 exhibited.
- **Renovate cannot see `-security` uploads** → It will not propose the upgrade, so the pin
  goes stale until someone notices. The kept `registryUrls` entry means this self-corrects when
  upstream lands `.xz` support.
- **Keeping unfetchable `-security` URLs looks like an oversight** → Mitigated by the
  `description` field naming the upstream blocker, so the config reads as intentional.
- **The repin tracks a security upload, so it may go stale the same way again** → True, and
  unavoidable without either the upstream fix or a scheduled check. The strict-equality
  dependency means this package is structurally prone to it.

## Migration Plan

1. **Repin** `android.Dockerfile` to `17.0.20.1+1-1~deb12u1`, verified by a `--no-cache` build
   of the apt layer. Unblocks cold builds. *(Done.)*
2. **Adjust `renovate.json`** on a `renovate/reconfigure` branch (drop `-updates`, keep and

3. **Sync the spec.** *(Done.)*
